page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-360 is a compute-focused instance powered by AMD EPYC 9B14 processors built on x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 360 dedicated virtual CPUs across 180 physical cores with multithreading enabled. Memory capacity totals 708 GB, yielding approximately 1.97 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include per-core L1 data cache of 32 KB, 1 MB L2 cache, 32 MB L3 cache, and instruction support for AVX-512 vector extensions including VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The hardware configuration includes no integrated local storage and no bundled GPU accelerators, requiring reliance on attached network block storage and standard CPU execution for compute pipelines. Benchmarks indicate exceptional multi-core performance, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 157,053.93 and top-decile results in stress-ng multi-core testing, Clang software compilation, and ray tracing. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 695.17 GB/s and write bandwidth reaches 344.03 GB/s, supporting high throughput in data-intensive tasks.

Cost efficiency is aligned with large-scale parallel processing where high core density minimizes overhead across distributed clusters. Workloads that match this profile include massive software compilation, batch encoding, high-concurrency static web serving, Redis in-memory deployments, and CPU-based LLM prompt processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-360 is a high-density, compute-optimized instance delivering 360 vCPUs across 180 physical cores on AMD EPYC 9B14 processors. Configured with 708 GB of system memory, the machine allocates roughly 1.97 GB of RAM per core, emphasizing processing power over memory capacity. Architectural capabilities include AVX-512 extensions with VNNI and BF16, hardware-accelerated cryptography, and 32 MB L3 cache. It operates without integrated local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core execution in stress-ng, PassMark CPU suites, Clang compilation, and ray tracing, while achieving an uncached memory read bandwidth of 695.17 GB/s. Static web throughput and Redis operations also place in the top decile. The platform offers strong resource efficiency for massive thread-parallel tasks, including automated build farms, batch processing, static web fleets, and CPU-driven prompt processing.
